message.content:
Here’s a quick mix of classic, cult‑favorite, and modern horror films that cover a range of sub‑genres—so you’ll have something whether you’re into jump‑scares, psychological dread, or supernatural chills.

| # | Title (Year) | Sub‑genre | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|--------------|-----------|--------------------------|
| 1 | **Psycho** (1960) | Psychological thriller | Hitchcock’s masterclass in suspense; the shower scene is legendary. |
| 2 | **The Shining** (1980) | Supernatural / psychological | Kubrick’s slow‑burn horror with an iconic haunted hotel. |
| 3 | **Halloween** (1978) | Slasher | The original “killer in a mask” film that defined the genre. |
| 4 | **The Exorcist** (1973) | Demonic possession | One of the most unsettling depictions of demonic possession ever made. |
| 5 | **Hereditary** (2018) | Family‑driven supernatural | A modern take on inherited trauma and occult dread. |
| 6 | **Get Out** (2017) | Social satire / psychological | Clever social commentary wrapped in a chilling thriller. |
| 7 | **A Quiet Place** (2018) | Survival horror | Silence is the main weapon; tense, inventive, and emotionally resonant. |
| 8 | **Midsommar** (2019) | Folk horror | Daylight terror in a Swedish midsummer festival; unsettlingly beautiful. |
| 9 | **It Follows** (2014) | Urban legend / supernatural | A fresh take on the “inescapable threat” trope. |
|10 | **The Babadook** (2014) | Psychological / supernatural | A metaphorical look at grief that becomes genuinely terrifying. |
|11 | **The Conjuring** (2013) | Paranormal investigation | Well‑crafted scares and a solid foundation for the Conjuring universe. |
|12 | **Paranormal Activity** (2007) | Found footage | Low‑budget ingenuity that sparked a whole found‑footage craze. |
|13 | **The Ring** (2002) | Horror‑thriller | A cursed videotape that still feels creepy today. |
|14 | **The Cabin in the Woods** (2012) | Meta‑horror | A clever deconstruction of horror tropes that still delivers scares. |
|15 | **Us** (2019) | Psychological / supernatural | Jordan Peele’s unsettling look at doppelgängers and identity. |

Feel free to pick based on your mood—whether you want a slow‑burn dread or a high‑octane slasher. Happy watching!
